drafts.label: Reply · UChicago analog Core
drafts.body:
I get why they want the room analog. A Core class is one of the last places a person is asked to sit with an idea without a tool finishing the sentence.

The ban on AI writing and grading only protects the hour inside the room. If the papers and take-homes still reward a clean final file, students will do the thinking with help later and the analog class becomes a performance. Keep the phones out if you want, but score the messy trail: the first attempt, the question they could not answer yet, a short defense in person. Otherwise we spent a lot of courage on a classroom rule and left the actual evidence of learning unchanged.
drafts.why: 440k-view education room. Do not retell the policy. Add what the ban does not score.
drafts.tip: Reply on the Maroon post, not a quote pile-on. Do not mention Anthropic. OP did not.

drafts.label: Reply · judgment is not leftover
drafts.body:
I keep hearing the same split and I do not trust it either. Judgment is not a leftover organ that survives after reasoning is automated. It is reasoning under incomplete information, with a cost if you are wrong about what matters.

If we tell people their job is taste, they will outsource the hard part and keep the vibe. The work is to make the call visible: what you weighed, what you discarded, what you would still defend tomorrow. Taste with no trail is just a mood. And moods are easy to fake.
drafts.why: Stay on his claim. No homework sermon.
drafts.tip: Talk to Itai about judgment and taste, not students.

drafts.label: Reply · AI CVs
drafts.body:
The guilt is pointed at the wrong person. If companies rank a PDF, of course people will use a tool to make the PDF look like every other shortlisted PDF. Not lying is the floor, not the skill.

The leak is that hiring still treats the document as proof of capability. A model can finish that document. Ask for a work sample they have to walk through, including a choice they would change. Until that is the filter, AI on the CV is just people answering the test we actually set.
drafts.why: Hiring-proxy room. Path is a work sample, not shame.
drafts.tip: Do not scold job seekers. Aim at the ranking of documents.

drafts.label: Original · analog is not the grade
drafts.body:
An analog hour is a gift. Phones out, sitting with the hard part, no tool finishing the sentence for you.

It still fails if the grade only sees the polished file later. People will protect the hour and then outsource the evidence. If you care about capability, the analog has to continue into what you score: the first attempt, the stuck question, the reason they changed their mind.

Would your last grade still hold if the clean version was taken away?
drafts.why: Belief plus a specific question. Adjacent to the UChicago room, not a retell of it.
drafts.tip: If the Chicago reply already says this, skip the original. Do not post both if they feel like twins.

drafts.label: Reply · educator · mastery line
drafts.body: I like this because it treats the essay as practice, not as a product. The leak I keep seeing is that students rarely get a clean signal for when they already know it well. If the only thing that gets a grade is the finished piece, they will use the tool on the learning step and still look like they mastered it. So the line only works if we also ask for the messy part: a first draft, the sources they actually opened, and a short defense of why they changed their mind. Otherwise we are still scoring the output and calling it growth.
drafts.why: Educator room with heat. Adds the missing mastery signal instead of retelling Willingham.
drafts.tip: Open Rod's post, then reply. Do not paste the assessment sermon onto Levie.

drafts.label: Reply · builders · workflow evals
drafts.body: This is the part I keep bumping into too. The public leaderboard tells you the model got smarter in general. It does not tell a company whether their actual workflow got better this week. If you cannot score the job as it is done inside the company, you will keep spending on inference and still be choosing on vibes. The useful eval is ugly and specific: the tickets, the documents, the exceptions that only that team hits. Until that exists, automation is a hope, not a measured step.
drafts.why: Big builder room. Stay on enterprise evals. Do not pivot to homework.
drafts.tip: Talk to Levie about company workflows. Human capability is the rhyme, not the lecture.

drafts.label: Reply · hiring · overlay
drafts.body: The overlay hiding from screen capture is the part that should make hiring people sit up. A live interview was already a thin proxy, and now a tool can finish the performance in under a second. Banning the app will not hold, because the next one will be quieter. If we still hire on polished answers in a 45 minute window, we are grading a show the model can run. Watch them work on a real ticket. Ask them to walk through a decision they made last week, including the wrong turn. That is harder to overlay, and it is closer to the job.
drafts.why: Professionals judged by a gamed interview proxy. Path is live work, not a ban.
drafts.tip: He claims not-for-cheating. Reply to the capture-hide and speed, not a moral scold.

drafts.label: Original · judge the middle
drafts.body:
We keep treating a clean deliverable as proof that someone grew.

The cost is that people learn to polish, not to think, because polish is what gets liked, hired, and graded. If you want capability, ask for the ugly middle: the first attempt, the wrong turn, the reason they changed their mind.

When was the last time someone judged you on that instead of the screenshot?
drafts.why: Belief post. Observation, consequence, response, specific question.
drafts.tip: Hold if it feels like yesterday's proof-confession. Post if the question feels live.
